title: Intervening at the User Input Stage: Does Flagging Loaded Questions Reduce Model Capitulation?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Clear causal chain: detect false premise before answer, apply higher epistemic standards, reduce sycophancy. Architecturally separable and deployable. Each link is explicit and actionable.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Building a false-premise detector (even as a prompted LLM judge) is moderately complex. The pipeline of detector + main model + evaluation requires orchestration. Feasible with mentor support but not trivial for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Requires building a detector, integrating it into a pipeline, and evaluating downstream sycophancy. Three distinct components. Could be scoped to just the prompted-LLM-judge variant, but still multiple moving parts.

novelty.reasoning: Several related works exist: retrieval-augmented premise verification (arxiv 2504.06438, 'Don't Let It Hallucinate') translates queries to logical representations and validates premises before generation. ELOQ (arxiv 2410.14567) detects out-of-scope questions. Linear probe methods flag sycophancy markers internally. However, the specific pipeline of a false-premise detector as a pre-filter that flags loaded questions and adjusts the main model's epistemic standards before answer generation has not been published as an integrated system targeting sycophancy reduction. The detection component exists; the integration into an anti-sycophancy pipeline is partially novel.
